Console evaluations only advise - every evaluation, allowed or refused, is written to the risk trail of the immutable audit ledger.

anomalies.title: Anomalies
anomalies.subtitle: Baselines are learned from this platform's own history - recorded evaluations, sessions, commands and incidents over a rolling window, never synthetic users - and describe how each principal actually works: their hours, devices, source IPs, targets, command verbs and privilege verbs. Every request from a trained principal is diffed against that profile; the deviations are named on the behavior component (5 points each). A CRITICAL deviation refuses the session start, ends the principal's standing sessions through the release-and-rotate cascade, rotates the credential the request sought through the real rotation pipeline, and records the incident below and on the risk trail of the audit ledger.

rbac.title: Role-Based Access (RBAC / ABAC)
rbac.subtitle: Five built-in roles over every admin operation: the admin token stays admin (everything), and a bound principal reaches exactly its role's operations. A local principal gets an API token once (vypam-rbac1.<id>.<secret>, sha256 at rest); an ldap principal is a directory username a login ticket carries; an sso principal is an SSO subject whose session bearer (vypam-sso1.<id>.<secret>) a SAML/OIDC login mints - in every case the directory or IdP authenticates, the binding decides (no binding, no access). Binding scope gates vault items and session targets. GET /api/v1/auth/whoami reports the acting principal.
